title: Waraqa the old cousin
hookLine: Khadijah takes him to her elderly, blind cousin, a man who knew the earlier scriptures, and the old man recognizes what came to him

cards: When something happens that nobody can explain, there's a kind of person worth finding. Not the loudest one in the room: the oldest one, who's read the most. The grandmother who's seen everything.
The professor who's retired but still answers the phone. Once her husband has stopped shaking, Khadijah takes him to see her cousin. His name is Waraqa.
He's very old. He's gone blind. And he has read the scriptures that came before.

teach.h: A CHRISTIAN WHO KNEW THE SCRIPTURES.
teach.b: The same hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari tells it. Waraqa ibn Nawfal had turned away from the idols of Mecca long before and become a Christian.
He could write in Hebrew, and had copied out from the Gospel as much as Allah willed.
Khadijah says: cousin, listen to what your nephew has to say. The old man asks: nephew, what did you see? And the Prophet ﷺ tells him everything: the cave, the grip, the word.
The old blind man recognizes it at once: this is the Namus that Allah sent down to Musa.
The Namus is the hadith's word for the angel who carries revelation, the keeper of the divine secret; Muslims understand it as Jibril. So Waraqa doesn't hear something new and strange.
He hears something old: the same messenger who came to Musa. Then he says something heavy. I wish I were young.
I wish I could be alive when your people drive you out.
The Prophet asks, surprised: will they drive me out? Yes, Waraqa says. No one has ever brought what you've brought without being opposed.

If I live to see that day, I will stand with you with all my strength. But, the hadith says, not long after, Waraqa died. He recognized what had come, blessed it, warned of what was coming, and was gone.
Muslims remember him warmly, as a man who knew the earlier scriptures well enough to know what he was hearing.

how: Muslims read the story of Waraqa in the opening chapter of Sahih al-Bukhari, and it is often told to show that the Prophet's message was recognized as belonging to the line of Musa and the earlier prophets.

games.q: you're Waraqa, old and blind. your cousin's husband tells you about a being in a cave who commanded him to read. what do you say?
o: this is the messenger who came to Musa.
games.why: this is the Namus that Allah sent down to Musa; and he warns that his people will drive him out (Bukhari).

practice: Think of the oldest person you know, or the one who's read or lived the most, a grandparent, a neighbor, a retired teacher, someone at your place of worship, and pick one question you'd truly want them to answer.
Picture asking it, then just listening to the whole answer without interrupting. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless your elders.

wordCard.voice: Waraqa. Khadijah's elderly, blind cousin, who knew the earlier scriptures and recognized the messenger who came to Musa.

orig.note: Arabic: the keeper of secrets; in this hadith, the angel of revelation.

carryVoice: Your line: the old ones recognize. Tomorrow, a silence, and then a surah of morning light. See you then.
